walkthroughs.body_html:
Eid al-Fitr means 'festival of breaking the fast'.

It celebrates the end of Ramadan. Muslims attend special prayers, share meals, wear new clothes, and give Zakat al-Fitr (a small charity gift) so the poor can also celebrate.

It lasts up to three days and is a time of forgiveness and gratitude. 🌙

Eid al-Adha is the 'festival of sacrifice', held during Hajj.

It remembers Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son when commanded by Allah — and Allah's mercy in providing a ram instead.

Muslims who can afford it sacrifice an animal; the meat is shared with family, friends, and the poor.

Jihad means 'to strive' — not 'holy war'.

Greater jihad is the inner struggle to follow Allah: resisting temptation, praying, studying. Muhammad called it the more important struggle.

Lesser jihad is the outer struggle — defending Islam under strict conditions (like just war: legitimate authority, last resort, proportionate, no harming civilians). Terrorism is rejected by mainstream Islam.
